text.p: Olympic medallist Anders Holmertz, one of swimming's most durable competitors, bade farewell to the sport with one more silver medal at the world short-course championships on Sunday.
He bowed out after swimming the second leg of the 4x100 metres freestyle relay in which Sweden were denied gold by Germany by a tantalising 0.14 of a second.
Holmertz was affectionately thrown into the pool by his team mates after the medal ceremony, clad in his blue and yellow Swedish tracksuit with his medal around his neck.
He clambered out, paused for photographers, then raised his arms and departed to the cheers of more than 5,000 fans in the Scandanvium indoor arena.

Holmertz, 28, figured among the world's top freestylers for a decade, bursting into the limelight at the 1987 European championships in Strasbourg where he deposed the great Michael Gross to win the 200 freestyle title.
He claimed another gold in the 4x200 freestyle relay at the 1994 world championships in Rome but an individual global title -- often tantalisingly so nearly in his grasp -- ultimately eluded him.
The Swede was a bold competitor who always went out fast but was denied gold time and again, paying dearly for the fierce and seemingly reckless pace he set when a rival overhauled him at the death.
He took silver medals in the 200 freestyle at the 1992 and 1996 Olympics and a bronze in the 400 in 1992. He had to settle for silver again in the 200 at the 1994 world championships.
Holmertz won 72 individual national titles and claimed the European junior 1,500 freestyle gold in 1983.
He has represented his country at senior level every year since then and competed at four Olympics. His European medal haul ran to one gold, one silver and four bronzes in individual events.
Perhaps inevitably it was silver again for Holmertz in his last two races, swimming the second leg in Sweden's 4x200 freestyle relay on Friday and again in the 4x100 freestyle relay on Saturday.
"I'm a bit disappointed. We were going for the gold medal," he said on Sunday.
He was given a rousing official farewell at the end of Saturday evening's session of finals with a presentation on the victory podium.
The crowd in the Scandinavium arena clapped and cheered as he made his way round the pool and waved farewell before returning on Sunday for a last silver encore.
